title: Crystallographic fragment screening in cancer and antiviral drug discovery: from electron density to translational outcomes.
one_liner_zh: 该综述聚焦晶体学片段筛选在抗癌和抗病毒药物发现中的应用，虽涉及转录因子brachyury等蛋白-DNA互作相关靶点，但核心是药物发现而非TF-DNA结合机制建模，方法上仅提及计算/机器学习辅助，缺乏AI或物理模拟的深度应用。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Crystallographic fragment screening (CFS) provides an experimental starting point for small-molecule discovery by defining a fragment's binding site, pose and routes for chemical elaboration. By establishing a structural hypothesis before major medicinal-chemistry investment, CFS reduces early uncertainty and the risk of pursuing a binding mode inferred from activity or modeling but not supported by experimental structural evidence. AREAS COVERED: This review examines how CFS advances fragments into lead series, preclinical candidates and clinical molecules. Oncology examples include kinase inhibitors, the PHIP2 bromodomain, the transcription factor brachyury and the metabolic enzyme PYCR1. Antiviral examples include viral proteases, polymerases, the influenza PA endonuclease and the SARS-CoV-2 immune-evasion protein Mac1. It also considers the practical requirements and limitations of CFS, criteria for hit validation and prioritization, and how high-throughput crystallography, reusable structural datasets and computational or machine-learning methods can support chemical elaboration and translational decision-making. Relevant literature was identified through targeted PubMed searches conducted from March to September 2026, supplemented by reference-list screening of relevant primary studies and reviews. EXPERT OPINION: CFS is most powerful when it provides an experimentally grounded binding hypothesis early in discovery. It converts weak binding into actionable geometry, reveals ligandable pockets and supplies credible design starting points. Computational and machine-learning methods can extend this information by exploring chemical space, ranking fragment elaborations and supporting multiparameter prioritization, but they do not replace experimental determination of binding modes or functional validation. Future progress will depend on reusable structure-affinity datasets and tighter structure-design-synthesis-test cycles that connect crystallographic evidence to biological decisions.
abstract_zh: 引言：晶体学片段筛选（CFS）为小分子发现提供了一个实验起点，通过定义片段的结合位点、构象及化学延伸路径。在重大药物化学投入之前建立结构假设，CFS降低了早期不确定性，并避免了基于活性或建模推断但缺乏实验结构证据支持的结合模式所带来的风险。覆盖领域：本综述考察了CFS如何将片段推进至先导系列、临床前候选药物及临床分子。肿瘤学实例包括激酶抑制剂、PHIP2溴结构域、转录因子brachyury及代谢酶PYCR1。抗病毒实例包括病毒蛋白酶、聚合酶、流感PA内切酶及SARS-CoV-2免疫逃逸蛋白Mac1。本文还考虑了CFS的实际要求和局限性、命中验证与优先排序的标准，以及高通量晶体学、可复用结构数据集和计算或机器学习方法如何支持化学延伸和转化决策。相关文献通过2026年3月至9月期间针对性的PubMed检索识别，并辅以相关原始研究和综述的参考文献列表筛查。专家意见：当CFS在发现早期提供实验依据的结合假设时，其作用最为强大。它将弱结合转化为可操作的几何结构，揭示可配体口袋，并提供可信的设计起点。计算和机器学习方法可通过探索化学空间、排序片段延伸及支持多参数优先排序来扩展这些信息，但它们不能替代结合模式的实验确定或功能验证。未来进展将依赖于可复用的结构-亲和力数据集，以及更紧密的结构-设计-合成-测试循环，将晶体学证据与生物学决策相连接。
